p: my heart's desire and prayer to: Purposing to set forth in the Jews an example of marvellous obstinacy, he uses this declaration.
For they: The first entrance into the calling to salvation, is to renounce our own righteousness by faith, which God freely offers us in the Gospel.
being ignorant of God's righteousness: The ignorance of the law (which we ought to know) does not excuse anyone before God, especially those that are of his household.
establish their own righteousness: Ignorance always has pride associated with it.

For Christ is the: The proof: the law itself points to Christ, that those who believe in him should be saved. Therefore the calling to salvation by the works of the law, is vain and foolish: but Christ is offered for salvation to every believer.

end of the law for righteousness: The end of the law is to justify those that keep the law: but seeing that we do not observe the law through the fault of our flesh, we do not attain this end: but Christ heals this disease, for he fulfils the law for us.
every one that believeth: Not only to the Jews, but also to the Gentiles.

For Moses describeth the righteousness which: That the law is points to Christ and is inclined to him is manifestly proved, because it propounds such a condition as can be and is fulfilled, by none but Christ alone: which being imputed to us by faith, our conscience is quieted, so that now no man can ask, "Who can ascend up into heaven, or bring us from hell?", seeing that the gospel teaches that both of these is done by Christ and that for their sake's, who with true faith embrace him who calls them.
Say not in thine heart: Do not think to yourself, as men that are doubting do.
But what saith it: Calling comes by the word preached.
word is nigh thee: By "word", Moses understood the law which the Lord proclaimed with his own voice: and Paul applied it to the preaching of the Gospel, which was the perfection of the law.

That if thou shalt: That is indeed true faith which is settled not only in the head, but also in the heart of man, of which we also give testimony by our outward life, and which serves Christ as our one and only Saviour, even as he sets forth himself in his word.
confess with thy mouth the Lord: If you profess plainly, sincerely, and openly, that you take Jesus alone to be thy Lord and Saviour.

God hath raised him from the: The Father, who is said to have raised the Son from the dead: and this is not spoken to exclude the divinity of the Son, but to set forth the Father's plan, with regard to our redemption in the resurrection of the Son.

believeth unto righteousness: Faith is said to justify, and furthermore seeing the confession of the mouth is an effect of faith, and confession in the way to come to salvation, it follows that faith is also said to save.

For the scripture saith: Now he proves the other part which he propounded before in the fourth verse, that is, that Christ calls whoever he wishes without any difference, and this confirms by a twofold testimony, Ro 10:4.

believeth on him shall not be: To believe in God is to yield and consent to God's promise of our salvation by Christ, and that not only in general, but when we know that the promises pertain to us, from which arises a sure trust.
For whosoever shall call upon the: True calling upon the name of God is the testimony of true faith, and true faith of true vocation or calling, and true calling of true election.
and how shall they believe in: That is, true faith, which seeks God in his word, and that preached: and this preaching God has appointed in the Church.
But they have not: Wherever faith is, there is also the word, but not the opposite, namely, wherever the word is, there may not necessarily be faith: for many refuse and reject the word.
all obeyed the gospel: He says this because of the Jews.
So then faith cometh by hearing: A conclusion of the former discussion: we must ascend from faith to our calling, for by our calling we came to the testimony of our election.
word of God: By God's commandment.

But I say: An objection: if calling is a testimony of election, were not the Jews called? Why should I not grant that, says the apostle, seeing that there is no nation which has not been called? Much less can I say that the Jews were not called.

But I say: The defender and maintainer of the Jew's cause goes on still to ask whether the Jews also did not know God, the one who called them. Isaiah, says the apostle, denies it: and witnesses that the Gospel was taken from them and given to the Gentiles, because the Jews rejected it. In addition the apostle teaches that the outward and universal calling, which is set forth by the creation of the world, is not sufficient for the knowledge of God: indeed, and that the particular calling also which is by the preaching of the word of God, is of itself of little or no efficacy, unless it is apprehended or laid hold of by faith, which is the gift of God: otherwise by unbelief it is made unprofitable, and that by the only fault of man, who can pretend no ignorance.
them that are no people: He calls all profane people "[them that are] no people", as they are not said to live but to die, who are appointed for everlasting condemnation.
bold: Speaks without fear.
